title: City contracts that say the payee holds money for someone else
question: Which City contracts describe the payee, in the contract’s own title, as a fiscal sponsor, fiscal intermediary or fiscal agent, and how much moved through them?
finding: 34 contract titles paid since fiscal 2019 use those words, $111.5 million in all to 19 payees: $92.3 million as fiscal intermediary, $11.4 million as fiscal agent and $7.8 million as fiscal sponsor. The largest: Healthright 360 ($77.7 million); Abode Services ($11.4 million); Community Initiatives ($7.8 million); San Francisco Study Center Inc ($5.5 million). In these contracts the payee is paid to pass money on, to people or to a named project, and the payment file stops at the payee.
how: Payments in the Controller’s vendor-payment file whose contract title contains “fiscal sponsor”, “fiscal intermediary”, “fiscal agent”, “f.s.”, a lower-case “fs”, “FS:” or a leading “FI -”, added up by payee and title. The short forms are read as fiscal sponsor and fiscal intermediary, which is a reading of an abbreviation, not something the file states; capital “FS” alone is not used because other departments’ titles use it in other senses. The role is read from the title. Titles under $25,000 and agreements with other public bodies are left out; a payment whose voucher number belongs to a year before fiscal 2019 is shown as 2018. The last column marks payees whose own tax return says they sponsor other projects (previous screen).
limits: Paying through an intermediary is often the point: the largest titles here are for writing cheques on a department’s behalf and for handling a named project’s money. The title words are typed by staff and are not a legal description, and the list misses contracts that do the same thing under a plain title. The payment file shows the money reaching the intermediary, not where it went next or what fee was kept. What would settle it: the contract’s budget (the administrative fee and the pass-through line) and the intermediary’s disbursement ledger. The payment file labels each line with a fiscal year that is not always the year the payment was issued: some earlier payments, mostly on purchase orders in multi-year capital funds, are filed under a later year, and the Controller's own published figures follow that label. Payments are dated here by voucher number, a single running sequence, which moves $5.52 billion of $119.3 billion (4.6%) to an earlier year than its label; $1.08 billion of that belongs to fiscal 2018 or earlier, before the file starts. Near the turn of a year the number dates a payment to within a few days.
